description: A single-panel classification/flow diagram (no axes, no scale bar, no legend) that sorts Fe-Mn-Al-C steels into two families and traces each family through composition, mechanical properties and application. The header "Fe-Mn-Al-C steels" branches left/right into two rounded boxes: "Multiphase Fe-Mn-Al-C steels" (Mn: 5-12 wt.%, C: ≤ 0.8 wt.%) and "Austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels" (Mn: > 12 wt.%, C: 0.8-1.2 wt.%). Below a centred header "Strength-ductility balance" the two branches continue: the multiphase box gives strength: 800-1200 MPa and elongation: 30-60%; the austenitic box gives strength: 600-1500 MPa and elongation: < 60%. Under the header "Application area" the left column ends with "automotive structural components reinforcements" and the right column with "automotive structural component, military". The figure's argument is a one-to-one mapping: the lower-Mn, lower-C multiphase grade trades a narrower strength window (800-1200 MPa) for a guaranteed ductility floor (30-60%) and serves as reinforcement, whereas the higher-Mn, higher-C austenitic grade spans a wider strength range (600-1500 MPa) with elongation below 60% and is additionally targeted at military use.
